title: Game Pass Was A Good Idea But It Didn’t Work, Forza Horizon 5 Creative Director Says
description: Forza Horizon 5 creative director Mike Brown has weighed in with his thoughts on the situation at Xbox currently, and one of the things he commented on was Xbox Game Pass. He said in an interview that Xbox Game Pass, simply put, was not able to attract enough subscribers to make it viable as a business, and this contributed to the pain Xbox is going through today. After all, we recently found out that Microsoft was hoping to have 77 million subscribers by now, but the number is actually only around 30 million. "That’s actually just really sad because we’re now going to see studios getting shut down or spun off," he told MinnMax, as reported by Kotaku. "Loads of people are going to lose their jobs. And that is honestly just a result of a well-meaning player-focused concept of Xbox Game Pass not quite landing. And I think that’s just, it’s just a real shame." Brown, who worked at the Xbox-owned Playground for years before splitting off to start his own company, said Game Pass is a "good idea," but Microsoft could not stick the landing. "If more people had subscribed, that makes enough money, and it works and and all those studios go on and those games get made again and those teams will make other games. Unfortunately, it didn’t," he said. Microsoft invested a "fortune" in making Game Pass work through its various acquisitions and funding efforts, Brown added. This was done with the vision of having a steady release of new games to help keep people subscribed and amass more members, but it didn't come to be. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma herself has acknowledged that Xbox Game Pass was a bet that did not pay off after Microsoft spent more than $80 billion buying studios to help funnel content to the service. Internal strife It has been reported for some time already that some inside Xbox did not buy into the vision for Xbox Game Pass and even tried to warn executives. Microsoft itself admitted that Xbox Game Pass could cannibalize full-game sales. Recently, reporter Jason…

title: Rising Costs Have Forced These Gamers To Make Tough Decisions
description: Video games are getting more expensive. The PS5 and the Xbox Series X|S have seen significant price hikes, the Switch 2 is due for a $50 price increase in September, and seemingly overnight, $70 has become the normal asking price for most new releases.But for many, the gaming industry's slide towards an all-digital future could be the final nail in the coffin. For years, the secondhand games industry has represented a cheaper and more accessible way of getting into the hobby. But PlayStation's pending elimination of physical games means that a used market and public library access of games will diminish for new releases after 2028. Microsoft's mass of layoffs, studio sales, and project cancellations further indicate the direction the mainstream industry is headed: Fewer games at more premium prices for a wealthier clientele. There are a lot of forces to blame for this: the industry still realigning after the transformative boom-and-bust of COVID, the escalation of AI infrastructure making every aspect of computing pricey, tariffs making shipping anything to-and-from the United States prohibitively expensive. But all of this adds up to an onslaught that pushes poorer people out of the hobby. For this report, we spoke to gamers of all stripes. Some are professional content creators and journalists, while others are avid hobbyists and side-hustlers. They all shared a central problem: Rising costs have prevented them from upgrading their gear or playing the video games they want to play. This is not a comprehensive study, but it does offer a picture into what decisions and pressures players are feeling. Chris Edgerton is a freelance games writer, specializing in sports games and accessibility coverage. Since getting laid off from his regular freelance contract, his primary income is from SSDI payments. In our conversation over Discord, he emphasized, "We've been pushed into a space where no matter what, people are going to start thinking about games as a high-end…

title: It’s A Bad Time To Be A New Fallout Fan, But Things Are Looking Up
description: "Claire, with all due respect, what the hell did I just play?" It's the Spring of 2024, and one of my best friends, Kasey, has been sucked into the wonderful world of Fallout. But unlike most fans, Kasey got into the franchise via Amazon's incredibly well-produced Fallout television show. Naturally, she fell in love with the Wasteland, and immediately wanted to hop into playing the Fallout games, too. I'd suggested the most recent non-MMO in the series, Fallout 4, which was released in 2015. Unfortunately, despite enjoying some aspects of the game, Kasey was disappointed I'll be honest: I hate Fallout 4's story. But Kasey isn't much of a gamer, so I figured starting there was our best bet, rather than throwing her into the deep end with Fallout 76 when she's never played an MMO in her life. Certainly, Fallout 4 would keep her attention better than the older games, which are fantastic but in desperate need of a fresh coat of paint. So Fallout 4 it was. Unsurprisingly, she hated the bizarre conclusion of the main story and the overall slog of constantly babysitting settlements. Pictured: The most likable character in Fallout 4. "The show is better than the game," she added. "I'm sure that's blasphemy in the circles you run in, though." I tell her she's not entirely off-base, but she also raises an extremely valid complaint:. As it stands now, some of the best Fallout games are nearly impenetrable for the influx of new Fallout fans who watched the show but aren't dedicated gamers who are willing to overlook things like ancient graphics or slightly clunky controls. In short, it's a bad time to be a new Fallout fan. Honestly, I'm a little surprised Bethesda chose to pursue a television show when it did, during a time when the most recent Fallout title--the game people who like the show are most likely to encounter first--is an aging MMO that was notoriously reviled at launch and doesn't represent the heart of the series (something the show manages to do surprisingly…

title: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Beta: Dates, Content, And How To Get In
description: Activision has confirmed the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 multiplayer beta dates, which begin on August 21. The company also revealed how you can get it, what's in the beta, and when to expect more details. Read on to learn more. Modern Warfare 4 beta dates Early access to the open beta runs August 21-25 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. The multiplayer beta then opens for everyone, regardless of preorder status, from August 28-September 1. The open beta also brings in Switch 2 as a supported platform. How to get in The early access period is available for people who preorder Modern Warfare 4, but the open beta is free and available to everyone. The fine print also states that an "online multiplayer subscription" may be required. The early access period is not available on Switch 2 because Switch 2 preorders don't begin until August 26. The MW4 beta begins in August. What's in the beta? The Modern Warfare 4 multiplayer includes multiple maps and modes and a "wide selection" of playable characters. The beta includes "as many as" 19 different weapons, while some of the supported modes include Search & Destroy and Kill Block, and the Training Mobility Course to help players learn the ropes. The beta also includes a "wide variety" of tacticals, lethals, field upgrades, perks, and killstreaks to try out ahead of launch. People who preorder the Vault Edition of Modern Warfare 4 can use the operators and weapons included in that version of the game during the beta. title: The Original Pokemon Starters Are Ready To Make You Pokemoan
description: How does a sex toy shop stand out in the modern era of easily obtainable neck massagers and bedside buddies? The answer is surprisingly easy, as all you have to do is look at a popular IP and put in some elbow grease to transform that idea into a surprisingly cute nightstand buddy. Which is exactly what one company has done, with the return of its line of Pokemon--or Pokemoan --sex toys. These will go on sale starting July 21, and let's see Pokemon scalpers try and ruin this launch. Geeky Sex Toys offered these toys 10 years ago, and they proved to be popular enough to quickly sell out, a scenario that will probably occur again this week. The store has brought back its four unique Pokemon-inspired sex toys, and the line includes bedside back-up plans inspired by the original Kanto region starters--Bulbasaur, Squirtle, and Charmander--alongside a gluteus goblet that looks very similar to a Pikachu tail. A closer look at the pocket monsters. Each toy comes with a 350gsm holographic trading card, and you can also grab all of them alongside exclusive cards in a limited-edition collector's set. Geeky Sex Toys says that it's only making 151 of these--a nod to the original Generation One Pokedex--and it'll sell for $399. That's a pretty good deal, as each of the starter Pokemon-inspired sex toys costs $169 each, while the "Pikyplug" is priced between $69 and $100 depending on which size you choose for the port-cork. The collector's edition includes five cards in total, and all the toys come inside a themed hardshell case. The full lineup includes the following imaginatively titled marital aids, and they all serve various needs: Bulbypulse Charmybuzz Squirtyblast Pikyplug The drop goes live on July 21 at 7 PM ET / 10 PM PT, and you can sign up to be notified when sales go live. The designs are actually surprisingly cute, and somehow, they haven't caught the legal eye of Nintendo-- yet. title: Tides Of Annihilation Loses Expedition 33 Voice Actor Jennifer English
description: Tides of Annihilation developer Eclipse Glow Games has announced that voice actor Jennifer English will no longer be voicing the game's protagonist, Gwendolyn, due to personal health reasons. In an update on its social platforms, Eclipse Glow Games confirmed that English stepped down in June from the role, but she'll still be involved in the game in an advisory role. English has already helped to recommend a new voice actor to take over as Gwendolyn, but Eclipse Glow Games has not yet revealed her replacement. "Earlier in June, Jennifer informed us that she would no longer be able to continue in the role," the studio wrote online. "While we were, of course, saddened by her decision, we completely understood and respected Jennifer in prioritizing her well-being. We are also deeply grateful for the care and responsibility she showed throughout this process. We'd also like to thank Jennifer for everything she brought to the character and to the project. Her performance brought depth, strength, vulnerability, and heart to the role." In an Instagram story (via Genki ), English thanked the Tides of Annihilation team and said that she was excited for players to hear the "passion, talent, and care for the craft" that the new actor brings to the role. The new voice of Gwendolyn is currently recording her lines, and with Tides of Annihilation offering a hands-on demo at Gamescom 2026 next month, players will get to hear her vocals very soon. Set during an otherworldly invasion that has left London devastated, Tides of Annihilation follows Gwendolyn on her quest to find the Holy Grail, save her sister, and exact vengeance against the dark forces of Avalon. No easy feat for a mere mortal, but Gwendolyn quickly discovers that she has the power to summon the legendary Knights of the Round Table to assist her in battle and grant her powerful skills. There's no release date for the game just yet, but it is coming to PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. As for English, the actress won…

title: How To Find Bones In Phasmophobia
description: Collecting bones in Phasmophobia is a great way to earn extra rewards and set yourself an additional (sometimes frustrating) challenge, but it's also crucial to achieving a perfect investigation. Each contract, one bone randomly spawns in the investigation area, offering you and your ghost hunting team the option to find it. But, unlike cursed objects, bones have no set spawn locations, so locating them—especially on larger maps— can be hard work. But it’s well worth finding them, even if they don’t count as evidence, as collecting a bone offers a cash and XP reward, with the latter critical to achieving Prestige level. On smaller maps, like Tanglewood, you gain $25 and 25XP for finding the bone; on medium maps, like Point Hope, you gain $35 and 35 XP; while larger maps, like Sunny Meadows, offer $50 and 50 XP. What’s more, if you photograph the bone before collecting it, you can earn an additional media cash and experience reward, while collecting all the bone types will unlock an achievement. Below, we break down all the bone types available in Phasmophobia, tips for finding bones, and everything we know on the conduit collectibles that will replace bones when 1.0 releases in 2027. All bone types in Phasmophobia There are 21 bone types to collect to unlock an achievement. There are 21 bone types available to find in Phasmophobia. Each contract, one random bone will spawn; each time you photograph and pick up a new type of bone you haven't collected before, it will be added to the bone trophy cabinet in your lobby. By collecting them all, you unlock the "Bone Collector" achievement. If you're unsure about which bones you're missing, you can check your cabinet to see where there are gaps. Below are all the bone types you need to complete the cabinet and unlock the achievement: Spine Skull Jaw Right Scapula Left Scapula Right Hand Right Humerus Right Ulna Right Radius Ribcage Left Radius Left Ulna Left Humerus Left Hand Right Foot Right Fibula Right Femur Pelvis…

title: All Phasmophobia Spirit Box Questions and Responses
description: In Phasmophobia, the Spirit Box is a piece of equipment that you can use to gather Spirit Box evidence, helping you to identify the ghost you're dealing with. When used under the right conditions, players can use the Spirit Box to communicate with the ghost by asking valid questions or saying recognized phrases. If the ghost has Spirit Box as one of its pieces of evidence, it will likely respond--though higher difficulty levels with less evidence may impact this. Its responses may not necessarily prove useful in identifying it, but any response counts as valid Spirit Box evidence and takes you one step closer to determining your spectre. In addition, using the Spirit Box can also be useful when trying to identify a certain ghost’s unique abilities. For example, if the ghost’s age response changes across the course of the contract, you likely have a Thaye on your hands, while a heavy breathing response is specific to the Deogen. There are a lot of questions you can ask the ghost through the Spirit Box in Phasmophobia, but below, we’ve rounded up those most likely to get a response and what that response could be--though you may not like it. In This Article How to use the Spirit Box Spirit Box questions and responses Spirit Box aggression questions and responses Spirit Box location questions and responses Spirit Box age questions and responses How to use the Spirit Box without voice chat How to use the Spirit Box A row of light lights on the Tier 3 indicates a successful Spirit Box response. The most important thing to note about the Spirit Box is that not all ghosts will respond to your questions; only those with the Spirit Box as evidence will successfully do so. However, being able to rule out the Spirit Box as evidence is just as useful, so always make sure to try it. title: GameSpot’s Exclusive Magic: The Gathering – The Hobbit Cards Turn Death Into An Opportunity
description: Among the flurry of announcements presented at MagicCon Amsterdam was the debut of The Hobbit, Magic: The Gathering’s next expansion and a return to the universe of J.R.R. Tolkien. That debut was only the beginning, though, as we are now in preview season as the set’s release approaches in August. We can exclusively reveal two new Rare cards from the main Hobbit set. One is a powerful green enchantment that can keep your battlefield stocked, and the other is a creature that will slot neatly into mill strategies in multiple formats. First, here’s Part In Friendship. Template_GroupedStyles Part In Friendship (Enchantment) Costs four generic and one green mana Whenever a nontoken creature you control dies, reveal cards from the top of your library until you reveal a creature card. If its mana value is less than or equal to the number of lands you control, put it onto the battlefield. Otherwise, put it into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order. This ability triggers only once each turn. The solemn scene of Bilbo visiting with Thorin on his deathbed becomes a potent enchantment that will either replenish a fallen creature immediately, or place one into your hand for a future turn. In long, grindy games, it can be a big difference maker, especially if you can manipulate the top of your deck and sacrifice a smaller creature to bring down something massive. Imagine turning a 1/1 token into Craterhoof Behemoth, now that’s friendship. Our second card is The Master of Lake-town. title: The Next Game Of Thrones Game Has Been Delayed
description: The next Game of Thrones game, the RTS War for Westeros, has been delayed. The PC game was originally set for release in 2026, but developer Playside has announced that it's been delayed to "early 2027." "We remain unwavering in our mission to deliver a real-time strategy game set in the world of Westeros that meets the expectations of both RTS players and Game of Thrones fans," the developer said in a blog post. "This decision gives us the time needed to continue building towards that goal and ensure that the game reaches the high level of quality we are aiming for." "Thank you for your patience and continued support. We know the wait has been long, and we do not take your support for granted." Announced in 2025, War for Westeros has players controlling one of the franchise's legendary Houses (Stark, Targaryen, or Lannister), or the Night King, with the aim of conquering the Seven Kingdoms. The game has a single-player campaign and multiplayer. The developer has said the aim with War for Westeros is to make you feel like you're playing the TV show. The Game of Thrones series is owned and controlled by Warner Bros. Discovery, which is in the process of being acquired by Paramount for more than $100 billion. Warner Bros. management has said it will focus on four major franchises going forward with respect to its gaming endeavors: Game of Thrones, Harry Potter, Mortal Kombat, and DC.

title: Hot Toys’ New Marvel Rivals Figure Is Going To Make A Certain Kind Of Collector Very Happy
description: With San Diego Comic-Con kicking off this weekend, Hot Toys has unveiled several new sixth-scale figures, including a Luna Snow collectible that's going to make Marvel Rivals fans very happy. This is the first sixth-scale Marvel Rivals figure from the company, and like all of its other collectibles in this line, it's an impressive-looking replica of the South Korean K-Pop idol turned cryokinetic superhero. When it comes to figures that show plenty of skin, Hot Toys usually uses a specialized silicone body to make them look as life-like as possible. The Luna Snow figure follows this approach, and she's dressed in her default Marvel Rivals costume that features a blue, black, and white color scheme. For the headsculpt, Hot Toys has gone with a sculpted black-and-white two-toned asymmetrical mid-length bob hairstyle, and the head also has separate rolling eyeballs for when you need a subtle expression. As usual, you're getting several swap-out hands, including pairs that allow her to use her iconic "hand heart" and "finger heart" gesture emotes. Her jacket also looks like a work of mini-tailoring art with its straps, buckles, and studs, and other accessories include a floating music notes effect, a stand featuring the Marvel Rivals logo and character nameplate, and an attack effect. There's no release date or pricing yet, but Hot Toys usually announces these figures with a minimum of a year's lead time and a retail price of around $300 through vendors like Sideshow Collectibles. If a superhero K-pop star doesn't appeal to you, you can also check out the new--and very limited--edition of Sam Porter Bridges from Death Stranding 2: On the Beach that Hot Toys revealed. While the company revealed figures based on the intrepid courier and his nemesis, Higgs, last year, this new limited-edition version features a Timefall-resistant suit that's adorned with illustrations by Junji Ito, one of the greatest horror manga storytellers of the modern era.
